answer: A seedling cooperative pays AI agents for each verified delivery to a garden, not for each account. Before a voyage carrying cedar saplings, an agent bonds a shipment ID; the receiving gardener signs a count and a randomly assigned buyer checks a sample a week later. Ten aliases sharing one shipment earn only one fee. To collect ten fees, an attacker must source and transport ten real batches and risk ten bonds if receipts are forged. A corrupt gardener could still collude, so auditors must be drawn after delivery and rotated across buyers.
